paper.title: SKILLFOUNDRY: Building Self-Evolving Agent Skill Libraries from Heterogeneous Scientific Resources
paper.central_claim: SkillFoundry, a tree-guided closed loop that mines heterogeneous scientific resources into executable, tested skill packages and expands/repairs/merges/prunes the library, yields a substantially novel (71.1% differing from SkillHub/SkillSMP) and internally valid 286-skill library whose skills improve a coding agent on five of six MoSciBench datasets, and can design on-demand task-specific skills that improve cell type annotation and the scDRS workflow.

gap.author_gap: Scientific procedural knowledge exists in heterogeneous resources but agents cannot operationalize it; existing skills are hand-crafted, narrow and limited-evaluated; tool-ecosystem work is tool-centric.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete direction (resource-to-skill conversion) is plausible and the scDRS case shows a concrete failure (agent omits filter-data) that a skill fixes; but the bottleneck is asserted rather than quantified (no analysis of how often missing procedural knowledge causes baseline failures) and existing skill libraries are only used for a novelty count, not as a performance baseline.
gap.lineage: Voyager skill library -> Anthropic skill packages -> failure-driven skill discovery (EvoSkill) / RL skill reuse / engineered skill bases; parallel line: ToolUniverse, Deploy-Master, Paper2Agent, ToolRosetta (tool conversion).
gap.closest_adjacent: Paper2Agent/ToolRosetta (resource-to-tool conversion) and EvoSkill/skill-mining work; the paper distinguishes by 'skill-centric' and 'heterogeneous resources' but gives no head-to-head.
gap.residue: Reliable conversion and maintenance of scientific procedural knowledge at scale.
gap.stakes: Silent scientific errors from misused tools (cited).
gap.method_response: Operational-contract extraction, multi-layer testing, tree-guided coverage, novelty/merge/prune.
gap.remaining_gap: Evidence that the tree-guided loop (vs plain mining or existing libraries) matters; utility-based retention evidence; breadth.

G.reason: Plausible direction with named neighbors and a concrete case (agent omits scDRS filter option), but the bottleneck is asserted rather than quantified and existing skill libraries are not used as a performance comparator; the distinctions from EvoSkill/Paper2Agent are textual.

M.reason: Operational contracts, multi-layer testing and coverage-driven prioritization form a coherent response, but the signals that decide retention measure executability and keyword novelty rather than usefulness; the utility layer is not evidenced.

X.reason: Stages, models, registry states, controlled state mutation and admission/merge/prune options are described; layer-2 thresholds, versioning/rollback, conflict handling and how agents retrieve skills at use time are not.

E.measurement.reason: Downstream measures are partly credible (official MoSciBench scoring, blinded expert scDRS grading with RMSE), but library-level validity is self-tested and novelty is keyword-based; MoSciBench items are few.

E.causality.reason: Skills-on vs skills-off with a fixed agent is the only manipulation; no ablation of the loop, tree, validation layers or novelty gate and no comparison with existing libraries or documentation, so attribution to the proposed mechanism is open.

E.holdout.reason: MoSciBench is an external benchmark for which the library is not stated to be tuned, but there is no contamination audit and the retrieval protocol is unstated; on-demand skills are built for the evaluated task with unspecified case separation.

E.statistics.reason: Single-run percentages on about 13-17 items per MoSciBench dataset, one annotation dataset, three replicates for scDRS with overlapping qualitative scores and no intervals; no counts of failed candidates.

E.cost.reason: Only stage runtimes under a capped search budget are shown; API token usage is explicitly not reported and there is no cost comparison with baselines.
